topic: similar triangles with a parallel segment
problem: In triangle ABC, point D lies on side AB and point E lies on side AC such that segment DE is parallel to side BC. If AD = 6, DB = 4, and DE = 9, what is the length of BC?

algebraFirst.description: Sets up 6/10 = 9/BC, cross-multiplies to 6 * BC = 90, and divides; the common trap pairs AD with DB = 4 instead of the whole side AB = 10 (giving 13.5 or 6).

explanationNotes: Explain why the triangles are similar: DE parallel to BC makes triangle ADE a scaled-down copy of triangle ABC that shares angle A. Corresponding sides are AD with the whole side AB (6 with 6 + 4 = 10) and DE with BC, so 6/10 = 9/BC; graphing each side of that proportion puts the answer at the intersection x = 15.
notes: Verified: BC = 9*10/6 = 15; distractors 9*6/4 = 13.5, 9*4/6 = 6, 9*10/4 = 22.5. Intersection of y=0.6 and y=9/x is (15, 0.6). Typing 6/(6+4)=9/x as one equation plots an implicit vertical line with no labeled point in Desmos v1.11.4, so it is not listed.
